title: Nehemiah: rebuilding the walls, and a people
note: Rebuilt on 2026-11-26 from the Bible Explorer film of the same slug. New wording, same facts: each claim is in the old film's captions or its 'differ' note, whose sources are in docs/work/elite/explorer-ledger.md. Scripture is the Berean Standard Bible, checked against client/public/bible/text/ by film/tools/write-script.py.

lines: Nehemiah was a Jewish official at the Persian court. In 445 BC he came to Jerusalem and rebuilt its broken walls in fifty-two days.
Much of the book is his own account, full of quick prayers and strong feeling. He's a layman for whom prayer and planning are partners.

scripture.text: When I heard these words, I sat down and wept.

lines: The book turns at chapter eight, from building the city to building the people.
First the burden and the night ride. Then the wall rebuilt against opposition. Then the law read and the covenant renewed, the wall dedicated, and the last reforms.

scripture.text: and they set their hands to this good work.

chapters.kicker: Watch for: pray, and keep watch
lines: Chapter three names who built each section: priests, goldsmiths, perfumers, a ruler with his daughters. Then come mockery, threats, and plots.
Nehemiah's answer is the book in one sentence.
So we prayed to our God and posted a guard against them day and night.

scripture.text: So we prayed to our God and posted a guard against them day and night.

chapters.kicker: Watch for: justice for the poor
lines: In the middle of the work, poor families cry out. Famine, debt, and the king's tax have cost them their fields and even their children.
Nehemiah confronts the nobles, and they give back what they took. A rebuilt city with an unjust economy isn't a restored city.

scripture.text: What you are doing is not right.

chapters.kicker: Watch for: the law read with joy
lines: The high point isn't the wall. It's the reading of the law. Ezra reads from daybreak until noon, the Levites explain it, and the people weep.
They're told to feast and share, because the joy of the LORD is their strength. Confession and a signed pledge follow.

scripture.text: explaining it and giving insight, so that the people could understand what was being read.

chapters.kicker: Watch for: an ending without triumph
lines: The ending has no triumph. Nehemiah comes back to find nearly every promise broken, and he acts, sometimes harshly. The text reports it without comment.
Nothing in it gives anyone today a warrant to strike or harm anyone. Walls can't make a people faithful by themselves.
Remember me, O my God, with favor.

scripture.text: Remember me, O my God, with favor.

lines: Start with chapters one and two. Then the key chapters: five, eight, nine, and thirteen. Listen for Nehemiah's quick prayers, and don't skip the lists of names.
Promises made in a great assembly have to be kept in ordinary weeks.
titleCard: Promises have to be kept in ordinary weeks.
